meta.title: LPKF Laser & Electronics — Klaus Fiedler's laser micromachining pivot through LIDE glass processing and semiconductor advanced packaging
meta.abstract: LPKF Laser & Electronics SE (LPK.DE on Frankfurt Xetra) is a German specialty laser systems company focused on laser-based precision micromachining for electronics, automotive, and emerging applications. The strategic narrative through 2024-2026 has centered on the LIDE (Laser Induced Deep Etching) glass processing technology for advanced semiconductor packaging substrates including glass core substrates emerging as alternative to organic substrates in AI accelerator packaging contexts, plus the broader PCB prototyping and laser welding systems business.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
The forward strategic narrative at LPKF Laser & Electronics centred on glass. Specifically, the company's proprietary LIDE (Laser Induced Deep Etching) process combined ultrafast laser modification of glass with selective wet etching to create through-glass vias and other deep microstructures without micro-cracks; by the frozen window, LPKF was advertising minimum feature sizes of 5 µm, aspect ratios up to 1:50 and panel-level positional accuracy on 515 mm × 510 mm substrates. That option value, rather than the legacy PCB-prototyping or plastic-welding franchise, was the feature that most clearly separated the equity story from a conventional German special-machinery cyclical. [LIDE technology](<https://lide.lpkf.com/en/technology/lide>), [NEXAR LIDE systems](<https://lide.lpkf.com/en/systems/nexar-lide>)

LPKF's shares traded in the Prime Standard of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the symbol LPK (ISIN DE0006450000). STOXX added the company to the SDAX effective 27 December 2024, but the regular December 2025 review removed LPKF from the SDAX effective 22 December 2025; the December 2024 change did not place the company in the TecDAX. The group dated its foundation to 4 August 1976, and its company profile said engineer Juergen Seebach developed the first mechanical process for creating printed circuit boards. Klaus Fiedler had served as CEO since January 2022, and the Supervisory Board extended his contract through 31 December 2028 on 23 April 2024. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [Deutsche Börse, 20 December 2024](<https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/nachrichten/selection-indices-unscheduled-change-in-dax-mdax-and-sdax>), [Deutsche Börse, 4 December 2025](<https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/news/selection-indices-aumovio-and-tkms-will-be-included-in-mdax>), [LPKF CEO contract extension](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-extends-contract-of-ceo-klaus-fiedler-until-2028>)

## Four Segments, One Strategic Pivot

The operating mix was more uneven than the existing draft suggested. In 2025, Development generated €27.1 million of revenue, Electronics €35.9 million, Welding €24.0 million and Solar €28.3 million. The previous year Solar had been even larger at €41.2 million and the segment's EBIT contribution of €5.7 million had made it the group's most profitable unit, while Welding was the main operational drag at –€4.8 million of EBIT on revenue of €18.6 million. Development demand was helped by delayed U.S. government-funded orders rolling out of the late-2025 shutdown, whereas Solar entered a sharp pause as customers weighed a shift toward perovskite cell architectures. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

## Financial Trajectory: Contraction Before Potential Inflection

Consolidated revenue fell to €115.3 million in 2025 from €122.9 million in 2024. Adjusted EBIT improved to €0.8 million from €0.1 million, but reported EBIT fell to –€13.5 million from –€2.5 million because write-downs and restructuring-related items still dominated the statutory result. Order intake fell 19.9% to €91.6 million, and year-end backlog dropped to €27.0 million from €50.9 million. For 2026, management guided revenue of €105-120 million and an adjusted EBIT margin of –3.0% to +4.5%. The first quarter showed the strain clearly: revenue fell 32.4% year on year to €17.1 million, EBIT was –€6.9 million and adjusted EBIT –€5.7 million, while order intake rose to €24.1 million and book-to-bill reached 1.4. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>), [LPKF Q1 2026 report](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/LPKF_Quarterly_Financial_Report_Q1_2026.pdf>)

In September 2025, the company launched the North Star transformation programme, aiming for a sustainable double-digit EBIT margin by 2028. The operational core of that plan was production consolidation: welding-system production in Fürth was shut down and transferred to Suhl, where solar systems were already being assembled. [North Star programme](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-strengthens-structural-resilience-north-star-initiative-aims-to-secure-long-term-profitability>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

## LIDE: Commercial Signals, Not Yet Commercial Scale

LIDE progress in the period was incremental but materially more concrete than in earlier years. On 13 December 2024, LPKF signed its first purchase agreement for several LIDE systems for series production of display applications, in the mid seven-digit euro range, with one machine scheduled for December 2024 delivery and the remainder for 2025. In April 2025, LPKF and Onto Innovation said Onto's Firefly inspection system would be installed in the cleanroom at Vitrion, which LPKF described as its center of excellence for glass processing in Hanover and a route to higher-yield glass-substrate production. In October 2025, LPKF said it had become one of the initiators of Fraunhofer IZM's 15-company Glass Panel Technology Group, launched on 1 October 2025 to scale TGV and RDL production on large-format glass panels. Separately, on 2 September 2025 the company said the Korean Patent Office had granted additional LIDE protection effective 1 September 2025, including the characteristic "earthworm structure" formed in processed TGVs. By April 2026 management said numerous semiconductor customers were using LIDE in test and R&D environments and that any high-volume advanced-packaging orders remained outside formal guidance because downstream qualification steps, not the LIDE process itself, were still pacing the ramp. [EQS ad-hoc filing, 13 December 2024](https://www.eqs-news.com/news/ad-hoc/lpkf-receives-order-for-series-production-with-lide-in-the-display-sector/b13f7624-08db-406d-af36-35ae5962c4c2_en), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>), [Fraunhofer GPTG](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-delivers-key-strategic-technology-to-fraunhofers-glass-panel-technology-group>), [Korea patent release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-strengthens-lide-technology-leadership-with-new-patent-protection-in-korea>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

> "LPKF is therefore consistently evolving from a machine supplier into a provider of functional solutions with disruptive technologies, clearly focused on growth markets." — Klaus Fiedler, 30 April 2026 [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

## What This Dossier Asks

The central question for LPKF is timing: whether LIDE glass-substrate demand converts from qualification and pilot production into recurring semiconductor-packaging orders before the cost reset in the core business has to carry the group alone. Secondary questions run through the Development franchise's resilience, the Electronics segment's ability to turn SMT and advanced-packaging positioning into cleaner earnings, the Solar segment's path through the perovskite transition, and the Welding unit's return to profitability after the move from Fürth to Suhl. Each thread is examined in the chapters that follow.

chapters.title: From 1976 founding through laser micromachining specialization to LIDE
chapters.body:
## Workshop Beginnings, 1976

LPKF dated its foundation to 4 August 1976. The company's own chronology said engineer Juergen Seebach developed its first mechanical process for creating printed circuit boards, which made the early business a speed-and-control proposition rather than a laser story: engineers could produce prototype boards in-house instead of waiting on outside etching shops. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>)

The first years were built around mechanical PCB processing, but the chronology also showed how quickly the company started moving into adjacent manufacturing tools. LPKF said it moved into its new headquarters in Garbsen near Hanover in 1991, presented its first StencilLaser system for SMD stencils in 1993 and went public in 1998 to raise capital for further innovation. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>)

## Milling to Photons

The laser turn became explicit in 1989, when LPKF said it developed a process for laser-based PCB structuring. A later company retrospective on the ProtoLaser family filled in the commercial sequence: the work began as a 1989 research project with the University of Hannover, reached market launch in 2000 with the first commercial ProtoLaser, and then broadened through the ProtoLaser 100 in 2004, ProtoLaser S in 2008 and ProtoLaser U3 in 2012. By 2025, LPKF was marketing the line as a mature platform used by research institutes, universities and industrial R&D teams for precise prototyping across FR4, RF substrates, PTFE, polyimide, ceramics and glass. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [25 Years ProtoLaser](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/25-years-protolaser-from-vision-to-precision-revolution-in-electronics-manufacturing>)

That development mattered because it defined the cash-generative logic of what later became the Development segment. The company profile still described Rapid PCB Prototyping as an in-house process used by industrial customers and research institutes worldwide, and the 2025 annual report said the segment addressed a global market of universities and industrial users through long-standing distributors. In other words, LPKF's legacy moat was not scale in commodity electronics manufacturing; it was installed process know-how in low-volume, high-urgency engineering work. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

## LDS and the Antenna Years

The next major commercial step came in 2006, when the company chronology said LPKF's Laser Direct Structuring process entered high-volume antenna manufacturing. That was the closest thing in the historical record to the turning point that made Electronics more than an adjunct to PCB prototyping. The process allowed conductive traces to be created directly on moulded plastic parts and aligned neatly with the handset era's need for dense antenna geometries inside shrinking consumer devices. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>)

LPKF's later annual reports continued to treat LDS as a core differentiator. The 2025 report described Electronics as the segment housing LIDE as well as laser systems for rigid and flexible PCB drilling and cutting, while the broader company materials still cited long experience in laser-material interaction as the common thread running from LDS into newer packaging applications. The revenue history also showed why the old antenna franchise still mattered: Electronics revenue remained €31.5 million in 2022, €32.7 million in 2023 and €36.9 million in 2024 before slipping to €35.9 million in 2025. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2023](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2023/LPKF_Annual_Report_2023_E_final.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2022](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/hauptversammlung/2023/EN/Annual_Report_of_LPKF_Laser___Electronics_SE.pdf>)

## Welding and Solar as Second Acts

The chronology placed another strategic expansion in 2000, when LPKF said it joined forces with a laser-plastic-welding team from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and opened new markets such as automotive. The business later hardened into a full Welding segment, and by 2025 LPKF was still describing automotive suppliers as important customers even as it pushed more aggressively into medical technology and consumer electronics. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

Solar followed in 2007, when the company said it started developing and manufacturing laser systems for structuring thin-film modules at Suhl. That line later became the Solar segment. The timing mattered: the existing draft treated Solar almost as a legacy runoff by 2024, but the disclosed numbers showed that it was still central. Solar revenue was €38.4 million in 2022, €39.5 million in 2023 and a record €41.2 million in 2024, before falling to €28.3 million in 2025 as customer investment paused around the anticipated shift toward perovskites. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

## LIDE and the Foundry Model

LIDE moved from laboratory promise to visible corporate platform in 2017, when LPKF won the Productronica Innovation Award for the technology and its Vitrion 5000 laser system. The award materials described LIDE as a two-stage process: local laser modification of glass followed by wet-chemical etching to create microstructures without micro-cracks or thermal stress. [LPKF LIDE award, 2017](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/news-and-press/press-downloads/2017/4341-pr-lpkf-wins-productronica-innovation-award-2017.pdf>)

The company profile then marked 2019 as the opening of the Vitrion Foundry in Garbsen, producing glass microstructured components for clients in the display and semiconductor sectors. That point is important because the public record by 2025-2026 did not portray Vitrion as a ring-fenced joint venture or separate listed subsidiary. The current Vitrion site described it as a brand of LPKF Laser & Electronics SE and a specialized foundry service for high-precision glass-based components and process technologies. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [Vitrion company](<https://vitrion.lpkf.com/en/company>)

By the frozen window, that foundry model had become central to LPKF's commercial story. In September 2024 the company said it was building a partner network around glass substrates and could support customers either by integrating LIDE into their production flow or by offering small- to high-volume manufacturing of glass cores through the Vitrion foundry. In April 2025 it announced Onto's Firefly installation at the Vitrion cleanroom in Hanover, and in October 2025 it said it had joined Fraunhofer IZM's Glass Panel Technology Group to help industrialize TGV and RDL processes on large glass panels. [LPKF partner network](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-builds-partner-network-to-innovate-glass-substrate-production-for-semiconductor-packaging>), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>), [Fraunhofer GPTG](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-delivers-key-strategic-technology-to-fraunhofers-glass-panel-technology-group>)

## The Late-Stage Portfolio Before 2026

The chronology also recorded the company's effort to diversify beyond electronics manufacturing. In 2015, LPKF said it developed Laser Transfer Printing; in 2023 it moved part of ARRALYZE to Boston, with ARRALYZE developing biomedical systems and solutions in Garbsen. By 2025, however, the annual report said LPKF had discontinued its own ARRALYZE activities and was reviewing a sale to a partner better equipped to commercialize the product. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

What emerged from the chronology was not a single straight-line pivot, but a series of waves. Mechanical PCB processing became laser-based prototyping; that broadened into stencil cutting, plastic welding and LDS; solar became significant and then cyclical; and LIDE re-centered the investment case around glass processing. By spring 2026, the historical through-line was clearer than the current draft allowed: LPKF had repeatedly tried to turn niche process expertise into new verticals, and LIDE was simply the largest and most capital-intensive version of that habit yet.

chapters.title: Development, Electronics, Solar, Welding plus LIDE
chapters.body:
## The Bench That Built the Business: Development

The Development segment supplied instruments of rapid prototyping to research institutions, corporate R&D centres and teaching universities worldwide. The business sat closest to LPKF's historical roots in PCB prototyping, and the company profile tied it directly to the original board-making franchise from which the group was built. The 25-year ProtoLaser anniversary release said the first commercial ProtoLaser reached the market in 2000 and that more than 300 ProtoLaser U4 systems had been deployed, underscoring the staying power of a laboratory-focused product family that was never meant to be glamorous so much as indispensable to engineers who valued iteration speed and process control. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [25 years ProtoLaser](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/25-years-protolaser-from-vision-to-precision-revolution-in-electronics-manufacturing>)

By the early 2020s, the segment confronted a structural question familiar to hardware incumbents: as cloud-based PCB fabrication services compressed turnaround times and dropped prices, the relative premium commanded by in-house prototyping equipment narrowed. LPKF's response was incremental rather than theatrical, centred on better software integration, higher precision and the operating cases where outside fabrication remained awkward or impossible. Development therefore remained a cash-generative support column rather than a high-growth engine, contributing €26.2 million of revenue in 2024 and €27.1 million in 2025. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

## Electronics: The Laser That Structures Three Dimensions

The Electronics segment housed some of LPKF's deepest intellectual property. Laser Direct Structuring selectively activated thermoplastic substrates to create moulded interconnect devices, a capability that found its most visible commercial use in antenna structures and compact electronics assemblies. The same segment also contained the group's advanced semiconductor-packaging work around LIDE, which meant it mixed a mature electronics-processing franchise with the company's most speculative growth option.

That dual character showed up in the financials. Electronics revenue was €36.9 million in 2024 and €35.9 million in 2025, a relatively modest decline compared with the violence seen in Solar. Management's first-quarter 2026 commentary pointed less to a completed rebound than to early signs of one: order intake improved significantly, especially in PCB depaneling systems, even though reported sales still reflected hesitant customer capital spending. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

## Solar: A Legacy Position That Still Mattered

The Solar segment carried the imprint of an older industrial cycle. LPKF's systems addressed laser processing steps for thin-film and other photovoltaic manufacturing flows, and for years the business had been treated as a volatile adjunct to the more stable prototyping and electronics operations. What the existing draft missed was that Solar had not already faded into irrelevance by 2024. On the contrary, it generated €41.2 million of revenue and €5.7 million of EBIT that year, making it the largest and most profitable segment in the group at precisely the moment when other businesses were struggling. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

The reversal came in 2025. Revenue fell to €28.3 million as customers delayed orders while evaluating next-generation cell architectures, particularly around perovskite-related transitions that management explicitly cited in the annual report and Q1 2026 release. That left Solar in an awkward strategic position: still large enough to influence group results, but too cyclical and externally determined to serve as the foundation of the equity story. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

## Welding: Automotive Adoption and the Polymer Bond

The Welding segment applied laser energy at the interface between polymer components, joining parts without mechanical fasteners, adhesives or the visual compromises associated with older techniques. Automotive applications provided the franchise's commercial foundation: lamp housings, sensor casings, control-unit enclosures and other sealed plastic assemblies all suited laser welding's combination of cleanliness, repeatability and dimensional control. The process also carried a secondary life in medical devices and consumer-electronics assemblies, where sterility or precision could outweigh raw equipment cost.

Recent disclosures suggested a business that was cyclical rather than broken. Welding revenue rose from €18.6 million in 2024 to €24.0 million in 2025, even though the segment remained a pressure point for group profitability during the restructuring phase. LPKF's own customer references stayed sparse, but the company did identify Schaeffler as one of the first adopters of its absorbing-to-absorbing technology for electric-vehicle cooling-system development in Dortmund, which helped put at least one named industrial user on the record before the frozen window. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [ATA press release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/laser-plastic-welding-successful-market-launch-of-lpkfs-absorbing-to-absorbing-technology>)

## LIDE: The Glass Bet

The technology that defined LPKF's forward narrative by the mid-2020s operated at a different level of ambition from any of the legacy segments. LIDE was not described in current company materials merely as a laser-drilling tool. LPKF's own technical pages presented it as a two-step process of ultrafast laser modification followed by selective wet etching, capable of minimum feature sizes of 5 µm, aspect ratios up to 1:50 and panel-level positional accuracy across 515 mm × 510 mm substrates. That specification set the basis for the company's claim that it could create through-glass vias, cavities and other microstructures for semiconductor packaging at densities that conventional brittle-material processes struggled to match. [LIDE technology](<https://lide.lpkf.com/en/technology/lide>), [NEXAR LIDE systems](<https://lide.lpkf.com/en/systems/nexar-lide>)

The commercial opportunity management articulated was the semiconductor industry's shift toward glass core substrates for advanced packaging. Intel's September 2023 glass-substrate announcement was the clearest public market-formation signal: Intel said it was on track to bring complete glass-substrate solutions to market in the second half of the decade because glass offered flatter surfaces, better thermal and mechanical stability and far denser interconnect design rules than organic materials. LPKF's own packaging materials made the same argument from the tooling side, positioning LIDE as one of the process routes that could make glass manufacturable rather than merely theoretically attractive. [Intel Newsroom](<https://newsroom.intel.com/artificial-intelligence/intel-unveils-industry-leading-glass-substrates>), [LIDE technology](<https://lide.lpkf.com/en/technology/lide>)

Vitrion, however, required a factual reset. The public record by the frozen window did not describe it as a separately disclosed joint venture or outside commercialization vehicle. Vitrion's own site said it was a brand of LPKF Laser & Electronics SE and a specialized foundry service for glass-based components and process technologies. LPKF's April 2025 Onto announcement called it the company's center of excellence for glass processing in Hanover. The implication was not that LPKF had ring-fenced the risk outside the group, but that it was trying to combine pilot production, foundry work and customer qualification inside a branded operating layer it still controlled directly. [Vitrion company](<https://vitrion.lpkf.com/en/company>), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>)

The chronology of commercialization was more concrete than the older draft allowed. In 2017, LPKF won Productronica's Innovation Award for LIDE and the Vitrion 5000 system. The company profile then dated the opening of the Vitrion Foundry in Garbsen to 2019. In September 2024, LPKF said it was building a partner network for glass-substrate production and could support customers either through equipment integration or through small- to high-volume manufacturing of glass cores. In December 2024, it disclosed its first production order for several LIDE systems for display applications, in the mid seven-digit euro range. In April 2025, Onto's Firefly inspection tool was slated for installation in the Vitrion cleanroom. In October 2025, LPKF said it was one of the initiators of Fraunhofer IZM's 15-company Glass Panel Technology Group, officially launched on 1 October 2025. [LPKF LIDE award, 2017](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/news-and-press/press-downloads/2017/4341-pr-lpkf-wins-productronica-innovation-award-2017.pdf>), [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF partner network](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-builds-partner-network-to-innovate-glass-substrate-production-for-semiconductor-packaging>), [EQS ad-hoc, 13 December 2024](https://www.eqs-news.com/news/ad-hoc/lpkf-receives-order-for-series-production-with-lide-in-the-display-sector/b13f7624-08db-406d-af36-35ae5962c4c2_en), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>), [Fraunhofer GPTG](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-delivers-key-strategic-technology-to-fraunhofers-glass-panel-technology-group>)

The uncertainty was timing rather than technical imagination. By spring 2026, LPKF said the majority of relevant semiconductor players were already using LIDE in development and qualification, yet it still excluded potential high-volume advanced-packaging orders from formal 2026 guidance because downstream qualification steps remained the gating factor. For a company that had generated only €115.3 million of revenue in 2025 and carried €27.0 million of year-end backlog, that timing issue mattered disproportionately. The legacy segments were large enough to keep the enterprise alive and technologically credible. They were not large enough to make a multi-year delay in the glass thesis painless. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, segment economics, capital allocation
chapters.body:
## A Reset That Hit Margins More Than Revenue

The financial record for 2022-2024 was materially different from the current draft's implied top-line collapse. Group revenue was €123.7 million in 2022, €124.3 million in 2023 and €122.9 million in 2024. The pain sat less in sales evaporation than in profitability and cash conversion: EBIT moved from €6.5 million in 2022 to €3.7 million in 2023 and –€2.5 million in 2024, while free cash flow swung from €0.3 million to –€11.1 million and then back to €1.9 million. Headcount rose rather than fell across that period, from 740 employees in 2022 to 761 in 2023 and 773 in 2024, which helps explain why the cost base lagged the softer order environment. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2023](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2023/LPKF_Annual_Report_2023_E_final.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2022](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/hauptversammlung/2023/EN/Annual_Report_of_LPKF_Laser___Electronics_SE.pdf>)

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (€m) | 123.7 | 124.3 | 122.9 |
| EBIT (€m) | 6.5 | 3.7 | -2.5 |
| EBIT margin | 5.3% | 3.0% | -2.1% |
| Free cash flow (€m) | 0.3 | -11.1 | 1.9 |
| Order backlog at year-end (€m) | 63.2 | 58.9 | 50.9 |
| Employees | 740 | 761 | 773 |

That pattern matters because it changes the analytical frame. Through 2024, LPKF was not yet a dramatically smaller company than it had been in 2022; it was a company whose revenue base had stalled while its cost base, working capital and strategic investment burden remained elevated. The squeeze was most visible in 2024, when personnel expenses rose to €57.0 million from €52.4 million and the personnel-expense ratio climbed to 46.4% of sales from 42.1% a year earlier. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

---

## Segment Economics: The Real Mix

The existing draft also understated how important Solar still was before the 2025 retrenchment. In 2022, segment revenue was Development €28.2 million, Electronics €31.5 million, Welding €25.6 million and Solar €38.4 million. In 2023, the mix was Development €29.0 million, Electronics €32.7 million, Welding €23.1 million and Solar €39.5 million. In 2024, Solar rose again to €41.2 million, Electronics to €36.9 million, Development fell to €26.2 million and Welding to €18.6 million. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

That last year is especially revealing because segment EBIT showed where the earnings strain actually sat. Solar generated €5.7 million of EBIT in 2024 and Electronics improved to –€0.9 million from –€2.3 million. Development dropped to €0.1 million of EBIT from €3.1 million, and Welding fell to –€4.8 million from –€0.8 million as automotive weakness bit harder. The 2024 story, then, was not that Solar had already been wound down; it was that Welding had become the principal operational drag while Solar temporarily carried a much larger share of the group than many investors associated with LPKF. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

By 2025 the mix turned again. Solar revenue fell by €12.9 million to €28.3 million after the loss of a planned major Chinese project and broader customer hesitation around the technological shift to perovskites. Electronics slipped modestly to €35.9 million, Development improved to €27.1 million, and Welding recovered to €24.0 million thanks mainly to a major project in Asia. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

---

## What Was Actually Disclosed on LIDE Spending

The public record was much narrower than the draft's estimate of cumulative LIDE spending in the "tens of millions." LPKF did not publish a standalone lifetime investment number for LIDE or Vitrion. What it did disclose were building blocks. In the 2024 group report, own work capitalized included €4.5 million of development services for products and software, and the parent-company report said €1.6 million was invested in intangible assets and property, plant and equipment in 2024, primarily IT/software and LIDE production at the Garbsen site. In 2025, group own work capitalized rose to €5.7 million. Those figures did not isolate the full LIDE cash burn, but they are the primary-source anchors available inside the frozen window. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

The Vitrion framing also needed correction. LPKF's current materials described Vitrion as a brand of LPKF Laser & Electronics SE and as a specialized foundry service for glass-based components and advanced process technologies, not as a separately disclosed Vitrion GmbH or a public joint venture. In September 2024, LPKF said customers could adopt glass-core technology either by integrating LIDE into their own manufacturing or by using small- to high-volume manufacturing through the Vitrion foundry. In April 2025, the company described Vitrion as its center of excellence for glass processing in Hanover. [Vitrion company](<https://vitrion.lpkf.com/en/company>), [LPKF partner network](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-builds-partner-network-to-innovate-glass-substrate-production-for-semiconductor-packaging>), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>)

That mattered financially because it suggested a commercialization model broader than one-off machine sales but still firmly inside the group perimeter. LPKF was trying to use foundry work, qualification support and adjacent process steps to create a larger addressable revenue pool around glass processing, while keeping formal segment reporting relatively conventional.

---

## Capital Allocation: The Disclosed Numbers

On disclosed capital allocation, investment in property, plant and intangible assets was €8.2 million in 2022, €7.7 million in 2023 and €7.5 million in 2024. That was not an especially heavy capex profile in absolute terms, but the cash-flow picture was tightened by working-capital swings and by the fact that R&D spending and restructuring costs were arriving at the same time. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

The most painful year was 2023. Net working capital rose to €40.0 million, or 32.2% of revenue, and free cash flow fell to –€11.1 million. That did not reflect a capex binge; it reflected a business whose sales held broadly flat while cash got trapped in inventories and receivables. In 2024 management started to unwind that pressure. Net working capital fell back to €37.2 million and 30.3% of revenue, and free cash flow returned to €1.9 million even though EBIT remained negative. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

| Capital and cash metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Investment in PPE and intangibles (€m) | 8.2 | 7.7 | 7.5 |
| Incoming orders (€m) | 124.3 | 120.1 | 114.3 |
| Order backlog (€m) | 63.2 | 58.9 | 50.9 |
| Net working capital (€m) | 26.0 | 40.0 | 37.2 |
| Net working capital ratio | 21.0% | 32.2% | 30.3% |
| Free cash flow (€m) | 0.3 | -11.1 | 1.9 |

The financing backdrop also becomes clearer when viewed through the later reports. In 2024 LPKF had a syndicated facility originally arranged at €40.0 million, including €25.0 million of liquidity and €15.0 million of guarantee lines. By Q1 2026, after renegotiation around the North Star transformation, the company described the facility as €25.0 million of working-capital liquidity plus €7.5 million of guarantees running through 31 December 2028. That extension did not remove the strategic risk around LIDE timing, but it meant the company entered the frozen window with more balance-sheet runway than the current draft implied. [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 report](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/LPKF_Quarterly_Financial_Report_Q1_2026.pdf>)

---

## The Real Financial Shape Going into 2026

The cleaner summary is that LPKF reached 2026 as a company whose revenue base had remained surprisingly stable through 2024, whose segment mix had been more Solar-heavy than the draft recognised, and whose real problem was the combination of margin erosion, uneven cash conversion and the need to keep funding LIDE while traditional end markets stayed patchy. The deterioration in 2025 — revenue down to €115.3 million, reported EBIT at –€13.5 million, order backlog down to €27.0 million — made the need for North Star more obvious, not less. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF FY2025 results release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-reports-slight-improvement-in-earnings-in-2025-and-initiates-group-realignment>)

chapters.title: Multi-year trajectory through restructuring and LIDE positioning
chapters.body:
## From Peak to Trough: The Revenue Arc, 2019-2021

LPKF entered the pandemic period after what was still the strongest year in the disclosed record. Revenue in 2019 reached €140.0 million and EBIT €19.2 million, implying a 13.7% margin. At the time, management was still pointing to a 2024 target of more than €360 million of revenue and an EBIT margin of at least 25%; later reports said that target, first published in February 2020, was withdrawn by the Management Board in mid-2022. [LPKF annual report 2021](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/LPKF_Annual_Report_2021_ENGLISCH_geschuetzt.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2022](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/hauptversammlung/2023/EN/Annual_Report_of_LPKF_Laser___Electronics_SE.pdf>)

The collapse in 2020 was sharp but not terminal. Revenue fell to €96.2 million and EBIT to €7.5 million. In 2021, sales slipped again to €93.6 million and EBIT all but disappeared at €0.1 million. LPKF said roughly €8 million of revenue was pushed from late 2021 into 2022 because of customer project delays and logistics bottlenecks, with more than €6 million of that slippage coming from Solar. [LPKF annual report 2021](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/LPKF_Annual_Report_2021_ENGLISCH_geschuetzt.pdf>)

| Year | Revenue (€m) | EBIT (€m) | EBIT Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 140.0 | 19.2 | 13.7% |
| 2020 | 96.2 | 7.5 | 7.8% |
| 2021 | 93.6 | 0.1 | 0.1% |
| 2022 | 123.7 | 6.5 | 5.3% |
| 2023 | 124.3 | 3.7 | 3.0% |
| 2024 | 122.9 | -2.5 | -2.1% |
| 2025 | 115.3 | -13.5 | -11.7% |

*Adjusted EBIT was €4.4 million in 2023, €0.1 million in 2024 and €0.8 million in 2025. The 2022 EBIT figure above follows the most recent disclosure in the 2025 annual report.* [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2021](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/LPKF_Annual_Report_2021_ENGLISCH_geschuetzt.pdf>)

## Fiedler's First Years: Revenue Recovery, Margin Compression

Klaus Fiedler took the helm on 1 January 2022. His first full year did bring a top-line rebound: revenue rose to €123.7 million from €93.6 million. But the latest annual reports put 2022 EBIT at €6.5 million and the EBIT margin at 5.3%, far below the 2019 peak and still dependent on a favourable Solar cycle. Segment data showed Solar revenue jumping to €38.4 million in 2022 from €12.1 million in 2021, while Development and Electronics remained far more subdued growth stories. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF annual report 2022](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/hauptversammlung/2023/EN/Annual_Report_of_LPKF_Laser___Electronics_SE.pdf>)

In 2023 revenue held roughly flat at €124.3 million, but EBIT slipped to €3.7 million and free cash flow turned sharply negative at –€11.1 million as working capital absorbed cash. The company nevertheless presented 2023 as a year of strategic progress and said it had narrowly achieved its forecast. On the reported numbers, that was fair enough: the operating base had not broken, but neither had it regained the profitability that the pre-2020 strategy once implied. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF reports strategic successes for 2023](https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-reports-strategic-successes-and-narrowly-achieves-forecast-for-2023-financial-year)

## 2024: Two Guidance Cuts and the First Statutory EBIT Loss Under Fiedler

By 2024 the strain became explicit. After nine months, LPKF cut its 2024 guidance to revenue of €125-130 million from €130-135 million and to an adjusted EBIT margin of 3.5-6.5% from 4-7%, citing investment reluctance, especially in automotive. [LPKF nine-month 2024 report](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-se-business-performance-after-nine-months-of-2024>)

The December ad-hoc was harsher. On 9 December 2024, LPKF said around €5-7 million of equipment that had been ordered or was due to be ordered for December would instead shift into January and February 2025. It cut revenue guidance again to €118-123 million and said it now expected only break-even on the basis of adjusted EBIT margin. The company also said it expected annualized savings of around €5-7 million from efficiency measures already being implemented with high priority. [EQS ad-hoc, 9 December 2024](<https://www.eqs-news.com/news/ad-hoc/lpkf-senkt-die-umsatz-und-ergebnisprognose-fur-das-gesamtjahr-2024/cd66d3c3-cdb7-456d-8add-d9058c1b7df6_en>)

Full-year 2024 came in at €122.9 million of revenue and –€2.5 million of EBIT. Adjusted EBIT was just €0.1 million, and the 2024 report said approximately €2.6 million of extraordinary costs, mainly severance and valuation effects on the long-term incentive scheme, weighed on the operating result. The segment picture explained why the earnings line failed even though group revenue barely moved: Solar still generated €41.2 million of revenue and €5.7 million of EBIT, but Welding slumped to €18.6 million of revenue and –€4.8 million of EBIT, while Development fell to €26.2 million and €0.1 million of EBIT. [LPKF FY2024 results](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-reports-results-for-full-year-2024>), [LPKF annual report 2024](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2024/LPKF_Annual_Report_2024.pdf>)

## North Star and the 2025 Reset

On 15 September 2025, LPKF launched the North Star transformation programme. The company presented it as a multi-year package to strengthen structural profitability and reduce the impact of revenue swings on earnings, with a group goal of a sustainable double-digit EBIT margin by 2028. At the same time it trimmed 2025 guidance to revenue of €115-125 million and an adjusted EBIT margin of 0-5%, down from the prior €125-140 million and 6-9%. [North Star programme](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-strengthens-structural-resilience-north-star-initiative-aims-to-secure-long-term-profitability>), [LPKF nine-month 2025 report](https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-publishes-9-month-report-progress-despite-challenging-conditions)

The programme did not merely rename a cost-cutting drive. LPKF's 2025 annual report and Q1 2026 update showed the operational consequences: production in Fürth was closed for welding systems and transferred to Suhl; the company said ARRALYZE's own activities had been discontinued and it was reviewing a sale of the product area to an appropriate partner; and the bank syndicate extended financing through 31 December 2028. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>), [Peter Mümmler CFO appointment](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/peter-muemmler-to-become-new-cfo-at-lpkf>)

The 2025 numbers captured both the progress and the remaining damage. Revenue fell to €115.3 million, adjusted EBIT improved modestly to €0.8 million, but reported EBIT collapsed to –€13.5 million because of additional write-downs and restructuring effects. Order intake fell to €91.6 million from €114.3 million, and year-end backlog dropped to €27.0 million. Employees declined to 727 at year-end 2025 and to 714 by 31 March 2026. [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 report](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2026/LPKF_Quarterly_Financial_Report_Q1_2026.pdf>)

## LIDE: The Option That Kept the Story Alive

The reason investors tolerated repeated restructuring language was the possibility that LIDE would eventually change the arithmetic. LPKF's public record showed a clear chronology. In 2017, the company won Productronica's Innovation Award for LIDE and its Vitrion 5000 system. In 2019, the company profile marked the opening of the Vitrion Foundry in Garbsen. In November 2021, LPKF entered a joint development agreement with a leading global display and semiconductor manufacturer; in December 2024, it converted that relationship into its first purchase agreement for several LIDE systems for series-production display applications in the mid seven-digit euro range. [LPKF LIDE award, 2017](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/news-and-press/press-downloads/2017/4341-pr-lpkf-wins-productronica-innovation-award-2017.pdf>), [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [EQS ad-hoc, 13 December 2024](https://www.eqs-news.com/news/ad-hoc/lpkf-receives-order-for-series-production-with-lide-in-the-display-sector/b13f7624-08db-406d-af36-35ae5962c4c2_en)

The commercialization model also grew more concrete. In September 2024, LPKF said it was building a glass-focused supply chain and could support customers either by integrating LIDE into their own manufacturing or by offering small- to high-volume manufacturing of glass cores through its Vitrion foundry. In April 2025, Onto Innovation and LPKF said Onto's Firefly inspection system would be installed in the Vitrion cleanroom in Hanover. In October 2025, LPKF said it was one of the initiators of Fraunhofer IZM's 15-company Glass Panel Technology Group for scaling TGV and RDL production on large glass panels. [LPKF partner network](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-builds-partner-network-to-innovate-glass-substrate-production-for-semiconductor-packaging>), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>), [Fraunhofer GPTG](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-delivers-key-strategic-technology-to-fraunhofers-glass-panel-technology-group>)

What the company actually claimed by the frozen window was also narrower and more credible than the existing draft's "more than 80%" formulation. Its company profile and 2025 annual report said the majority of relevant players in the semiconductor market were already using LIDE in development and qualification. The same materials said the breakthrough to mass production was the next milestone, not an accomplished fact. When LPKF issued 2026 guidance, it explicitly excluded potential high-volume advanced-packaging orders because the timing depended on qualification of downstream process steps. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>), [LPKF Q1 2026 release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-gets-off-to-a-solid-start-in-2026>)

## The Equation Facing 2028

By spring 2026, the earnings story was therefore not one clean turnaround but two overlapping narratives. The first was a conventional restructuring programme around a business still large enough to matter in PCB prototyping, SMT, welding and solar, but not yet profitable enough to self-fund every ambition comfortably. The second was a glass-processing option whose market logic looked real, but whose timing remained outside management's direct control.

That is why 2028 mattered so much in the company narrative. North Star set the deadline for a double-digit EBIT ambition; Fiedler's contract ran to the end of that same year; and the advanced-packaging roadmap still depended on customer qualification cycles that LPKF itself repeatedly said were the gating item. The symbolically important part — winning the first production display order — had already happened. The still-missing part was repeatable, disclosed volume.

chapters.title: Klaus Fiedler, Management Board, Supervisory Board
chapters.body:
## The Architecture of German Two-Tier Control

LPKF Laser & Electronics SE — registered under the *Societas Europaea* corporate form — has a two-board structure reconstituted since 2022. The Management Board stood at two members by the frozen snapshot date. The Supervisory Board added fresh expertise in technology and financial audit through elections between 2023 and 2025, aligning structurally with the company's pivot toward higher-complexity, higher-margin opportunities.

---

## Klaus Fiedler: A CEO Built for the Transformation

Dr. Klaus Fiedler, born in 1971, assumed the Chief Executive role in January 2022, taking charge of a company that had just navigated a volatile pandemic-era demand surge and was beginning to articulate a more focused strategic identity. His appointment was extended through December 31, 2028 — a six-year horizon that, if served in full, would make him the steward of LPKF across the critical period when its LIDE glass-substrate technology was expected either to reach commercial inflection or to clarify the limits of its addressable market.

Under LPKF's assignment of Management Board responsibilities, Fiedler's portfolio was sweeping rather than narrow. He held direct oversight of strategy, sales and marketing, human resources, manufacturing, research and development, and innovation — in effect, everything upstream of the balance sheet. That breadth was partly a function of a two-member board where functional responsibility has to be split cleanly; it was also a signal that Fiedler was hired as a transformation executive, not merely a caretaker of a mature industrial franchise.

Fiedler came to LPKF with an academic engineering foundation — the doctoral prefix indicating technical depth appropriate for a company whose commercial moat rests on laser physics and precision micro-machining know-how. His mandate from the outset was to refocus LPKF away from the revenue and margin dispersion that had accumulated across its legacy portfolio and toward growth segments where laser expertise translated into durable differentiation.

The vehicle for that transformation acquired a name: **North Star**. By 2025, LPKF was publicly describing the programme as the framework driving its group restructuring, with Advanced Semicon Packaging — the division that houses the LIDE glass-processing technology — identified as showing "good progress" even as the broader company navigated uneven demand across its other segments. For Fiedler personally, the LIDE trajectory represented the highest-stakes bet of his tenure. Glass core substrates, positioned as a potential successor to organic substrates for high-end semiconductor packages, offered a market opportunity with a scale that dwarfed LPKF's traditional PCB-prototyping or welding revenue lines. Whether his allocation of capital and organisational energy toward that opportunity would be vindicated remained, as of May 2026, an open question — but the commercial signals through Q1 2026, with a group book-to-bill ratio of 1.4, offered at least near-term encouragement.

---

## Peter Mümmler: A New CFO and a Leaner Board

The appointment of **Peter Mümmler** as Chief Financial Officer in April 2025, with a term running through March 2028, introduced new financial stewardship at a moment when LPKF was simultaneously restructuring and investing. Born in 1968, Mümmler took responsibility for finance, controlling, digital systems and IT, and legal and compliance — the balance-sheet and operational-infrastructure complement to Fiedler's commercial and technology mandate.

The two-member configuration of the Management Board was itself a structural choice. Larger German industrial companies often distribute operational authority across three or four Vorstand members, with dedicated portfolio managers for international operations or individual business divisions. LPKF's slimmer arrangement concentrated accountability and streamlined decision-making — important for a company that, under North Star, was attempting to accelerate strategic decisions while holding down costs. The risk of that configuration is execution strain; its benefit is clarity of command.

Mümmler's 2025 arrival marked a transition at the CFO level. His predecessor had shepherded the company through the post-pandemic cycle and the initial phases of LIDE investment; Mümmler inherited a balance sheet being actively reshaped by restructuring charges and capital commitments to the Vitrion glass foundry build-out.

---

## The Supervisory Board: Five Members, Three Cohorts

By the snapshot date, LPKF's Supervisory Board comprised five members — all considered independent of the Management Board by the company's own assessment, and operating without a controlling shareholder whose preferences might subordinate minority interests. The board was organised into two standing committees: an **Audit, Risk and ESG Committee** and a **Remuneration and Nomination Committee**.

The longest-serving member was **Dr. Dirk Rothweiler**, born in 1963, who had served as Deputy Chairman since June 2019 and as a board member since June 2017. An independent management consultant, Rothweiler brought the kind of general executive experience that anchors remuneration discussions; he sat on the Remuneration and Nomination Committee alongside Chairwoman Alexa Siebert.

**Prof. Dr.-Ing. Ludger Overmeyer**, born in 1964, occupied the board's scientific and engineering pole. A professor and institute head at Leibniz University Hanover — geographically proximate to LPKF's Garbsen headquarters — Overmeyer joined the board in June 2019 and was re-elected through 2028. His academic specialism in production technology and logistics systems gave the Supervisory Board a lens capable of interrogating the technical feasibility claims that underpin LPKF's investment case, particularly on the LIDE side.

**Alexa Siebert**, born in 1970, joined as a member in June 2023 and was elevated to Supervisory Board Chairwoman on June 4, 2025. She chairs the Audit, Risk and ESG Committee and serves on the Remuneration and Nomination Committee — a combination that positions her as the central governance anchor of the oversight structure. The elevation of Siebert to the chair role in 2025, the same year the company intensified its restructuring and the same AGM that seated a new member, signalled a board that was repositioning for a more demanding operating environment.

**Anka Wittenberg**, born in 1963, joined in May 2023 and chairs the Remuneration and Nomination Committee — the body responsible for Management Board compensation design and succession. Her dual presence on the Audit, Risk and ESG Committee reflected the board's small size and the resulting need for members to serve across functions.

The newest arrival was **Paul Owsianowski**, born in 1987, elected at the June 2025 AGM. At 37 or 38 years old at the snapshot date, Owsianowski represented the youngest perspective on the board, seated on the Audit, Risk and ESG Committee alongside Siebert and Wittenberg. His election coincided with the update to LPKF's Articles of Incorporation in June 2025, a further signal that the board's composition and governing documents were being refreshed in step with the company's strategic evolution.

---

## LIDE, Vitrion, and the Question of Segment Leadership

Below Management Board level, the LIDE glass-processing franchise operated through **Vitrion**, a dedicated division positioned as an end-to-end glass-processing foundry service under the branding *Vitrion® by LPKF®*. LPKF was the inventor of both the LIDE® laser-induced deep-etching process and the Tensor® Bonding methodology, which together formed the technological foundation of Vitrion's glass microstructuring capabilities.

The division served markets including MEMS, RF technologies, photonic systems and semiconductor advanced packaging. The public record by the frozen window was not as opaque as the draft implied: LIDE-related releases quoted Dr. Roman Ostholt as Managing Director LIDE in September 2025 and as Managing Director Electronics in October 2025, while the Vitrion site identified Dr. Rafael Santos as Director of Technical Sales and Dr.-Ing. Maik Bertke as Product & Process Manager. That suggested a small specialist operating layer beneath Fiedler and Mümmler rather than an unnamed project office. [Korea patent release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-strengthens-lide-technology-leadership-with-new-patent-protection-in-korea>), [Fraunhofer GPTG](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/lpkf-delivers-key-strategic-technology-to-fraunhofers-glass-panel-technology-group>), [Vitrion company](<https://vitrion.lpkf.com/en/company>)

---

## Governance Alignment with Strategic Risk

The governance architecture that Fiedler and the reconstituted Supervisory Board had assembled by mid-2026 was calibrated for a company in transition. The Management Board was small enough to move quickly; the Supervisory Board's independence, its refreshed membership, and its committee structure provided the oversight framework that LPKF's Prime Standard listing on Deutsche Börse — and its obligations under the German Corporate Governance Code — demanded.

The critical variable was whether the board's oversight mechanisms were well-matched to the asymmetric nature of the LIDE opportunity: a technology investment whose full commercial return lay beyond the normal two-to-three-year horizon of annual target-setting, requiring patient capital stewardship and an oversight body capable of distinguishing developmental setbacks from strategic failure. Overmeyer's technical profile, Siebert's audit and risk focus, and Fiedler's mandate extending through 2028 together suggested that LPKF had deliberately constructed the conditions for a long-duration technology bet — even if the market, quarter by quarter, continued to demand shorter-cycle evidence of progress.

---

*Primary sources: [LPKF Laser & Electronics SE — Management](https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/management); [LPKF Corporate Governance](https://www.lpkf.com/en/investor-relations/corporate-governance/); [Vitrion by LPKF](https://vitrion.lpkf.com/en/); [LPKF Corporate News](https://www.lpkf.com/en/investor-relations/publications/corporate-news); Frankfurt Stock Exchange, LPK.*

chapters.title: PCB prototyping customers, automotive welding, electronics, emerging LIDE
chapters.body:
## The Foundation: PCB Prototyping's Global Laboratory Network

The Development segment had by the mid-2020s built a broad installed base across laboratories worldwide. Research institutes, university departments and industrial R&D groups remained the natural customer base, and the company's own materials continued to frame rapid in-house prototyping as a standard tool for both research and production engineering. [LPKF company profile](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/company/company-profile>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>) The customer profile was deliberately diffuse: aerospace contractors, automotive electronics R&D centers, and university engineering departments. Defense and aerospace customers valued the self-sufficiency — classified circuit designs could stay behind the facility perimeter. Application support engineers reinforced retention and generated consumables revenue. The segment provided predictable cash flow and global brand recognition that could support cross-selling as the portfolio expanded.

## Automotive Plastic Welding: The Tier-1 Supply Chain Relationship

The Welding segment tied closely to lightweight thermoplastic assemblies — tail-lamp housings, sensor enclosures, ADAS module housings and other sealed electronics casings. Before the frozen window, LPKF rarely named production customers in its core welding franchise, but it did identify the Schaeffler Group as one of the first adopters of its ATA process, using it in Dortmund for the development of electric-vehicle cooling systems. More broadly, the 2025 annual report said automotive suppliers remained important customers even as the segment reoriented toward medical technology and consumer electronics. [ATA press release](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/laser-plastic-welding-successful-market-launch-of-lpkfs-absorbing-to-absorbing-technology>), [LPKF annual report 2025](<https://www.lpkf.com/fileadmin/mediafiles/user_upload/company/investor-relations/financial-reports/2025/LPKF_Annual_Report_2025.pdf>)

The electric vehicle transition created a secondary demand layer. EV architectures carried more sealed electronic control units, battery management modules, and power electronics housings than their internal combustion equivalents, and each of those assemblies required a joining process. Laser plastic welding competed with ultrasonic welding and vibration welding in this space, with laser technology offering advantages in joint quality and process control visibility — arguments LPKF's application engineers made frequently to automotive procurement teams through the early 2020s.

Revenue from the Welding segment tracked automotive production volumes with a lag, meaning the supply chain disruptions of 2021-2022 created irregular order patterns that management acknowledged in investor communications. By 2023-2024, as automotive production partially normalized, the segment returned to steadier order intake, though the broader European automotive demand softening — driven by the slower-than-projected EV uptake and inventory corrections at German OEMs — created renewed headwinds that management was navigating through the restructuring cycle.

## Laser Direct Structuring: The Smartphone Antenna Chapter and Its Aftermath

The Electronics segment's defining product line was Laser Direct Structuring (LDS), commercialized under the LPKF Multiline brand, which enabled circuit traces to be patterned directly onto three-dimensionally molded plastic parts. The technology created Molded Interconnect Devices (MIDs), and its most significant application was the integration of cellular antenna structures into smartphone housings and interior plastic frames.

The LDS antenna era shaped LPKF's financial trajectory through the 2013-2019 period. As smartphone OEMs crammed more frequency bands — and ultimately 5G sub-6GHz and millimeter-wave capability — into thinning handset profiles, LDS-structured three-dimensional antenna forms offered spatial efficiency that flat-antenna designs could not match. LPKF's systems processed the plastic substrates; LPKF's proprietary laser-activatable additive was compounded into the plastic; and the antenna patterns were then metallized by the contract manufacturer's plating line. The company's LDS equipment and materials were integrated into the supply chains of antenna component suppliers serving multiple major handset brands.

The segment's revenue, however, proved volatile. As handset makers standardized their antenna designs and competing processes — flexible printed circuits, direct printing — gained traction, LDS pricing came under pressure and capital equipment order patterns became lumpy. LPKF invested in broadening LDS applications into medical device interconnects, industrial IoT sensor housings, and automotive radar modules, but none of those adjacencies replicated the volume density that smartphone antenna had provided at its peak. By the mid-2020s, the Electronics segment was a stable contributor rather than a high-growth engine, with LPKF positioning LDS in its investor materials primarily as a technology demonstrating the company's core competence in laser-materials interaction rather than a primary revenue growth driver.

## LIDE: The Glass Substrate Option

Against that backdrop of mature-segment stability, LPKF's most consequential strategic development heading into the late 2020s was Laser Induced Deep Etching — LIDE. The process uses ultrashort-pulse laser exposure followed by a wet chemical etch to create high-aspect-ratio microstructures in glass substrates: through-glass vias, precision cavities, and shaped glass panels with tolerances measured in single-digit microns.

The commercial opportunity LPKF's management articulated was the semiconductor industry's nascent shift toward glass core substrates for advanced packaging. Organic substrates — the laminate boards on which logic dies and memory packages are assembled in high-performance processors and AI accelerators — faced physical limits in routing density and thermal performance. Glass, with superior dimensional stability, lower coefficient of thermal expansion, and electrical properties compatible with high-speed signaling, had attracted the attention of major semiconductor companies exploring next-generation packaging architectures.

Vitrion was the vehicle LPKF used to commercialize LIDE at foundry level, but the public description was more specific than the draft suggested: Vitrion described itself as a brand of LPKF Laser & Electronics SE and as a specialized foundry service for glass-based components and process technologies. LPKF's own releases also used the name for its glass-processing center of excellence in Hanover and for the route through which customer sampling, pilot work and small-series production could be handled inside the group. [Vitrion company](<https://vitrion.lpkf.com/en/company>), [Onto Innovation / LPKF](<https://www.lpkf.com/en/news-press/press-releases-teaser/onto-innovation-and-lpkf-are-set-to-accelerate-mass-production-of-glass-core-substrates-for-semiconductors>)

LPKF's Garbsen facility housed the LIDE technology development and early production capability. The manufacturing footprint in Garbsen — the headquarters site that had served as the company's primary engineering and production base for decades — thus carried dual responsibility: sustaining the existing PCB prototyping, welding, and electronics equipment businesses while hosting the advanced glass processing work that management believed could become a disproportionate contributor to enterprise value over a multi-year horizon.

## Germany Manufacturing: Garbsen as the Hub

The Garbsen facility, situated in the Hannover metropolitan area in Lower Saxony, reflected LPKF's roots as a precision engineering company embedded in Germany's Mittelstand industrial tradition. The site combined mechanical engineering, laser optics assembly, process application laboratories, and global customer support operations within a campus that had expanded incrementally as the product portfolio grew.

LPKF complemented Garbsen with regional subsidiaries in North America, Asia-Pacific, and elsewhere, primarily organized as sales and application support operations rather than manufacturing centers. The production concentration in Germany meant that Garbsen-based engineering and manufacturing costs were denominated in euros and subject to German labor market dynamics — a structural consideration that the 2023-2024 operational restructuring program addressed through headcount and process efficiency initiatives management communicated to Frankfurt Xetra investors in their restructuring disclosures.

The strategic logic of maintaining German manufacturing — rather than pursuing Asian production-cost arbitrage — rested on the precision-engineering content of LPKF's systems and the intellectual property embedded in laser optics, control software, and process recipes that would be difficult to protect at arm's-length contract manufacturing relationships. For LIDE specifically, the technology sensitivity reinforced the case for keeping production capability close to the Garbsen engineering center through the commercial development phase.

chapters.title: Where LPKF sits in laser micromachining, PCB prototyping, glass processing
chapters.body:
## A Specialist in a Field of Giants

LPKF occupies an unusual address: a mid-cap specialist holding dominant or near-dominant positions in markets small enough that the giants rarely bother to show up. Its three principal competitive theatres — laser micromachining broadly, benchtop PCB prototyping, and nascent glass-substrate processing via LIDE — each have distinct dynamics telling different stories about moat depth and growth durability.

## Laser Micromachining: Competing Where Trumpf Does Not

The laser titans — Trumpf, IPG Photonics and Coherent — were not the cleanest day-to-day comparators because their center of gravity remained in much larger industrial laser markets. The nearer micromachining peer set was more specialized. LASEA's own materials described a Liège-based group focused on high-precision laser solutions for medical devices, aerospace components, watchmaking, semiconductors and electronics, with engineering, R&D and system integration anchored in Belgium. That made it a real ultrafast-laser reference point, but not a public pure-play on glass-core-substrate industrialization. [LASEA about us](<https://lasea.com/about-us/>), [LASEA applications](<https://lasea.com/applications/>)

**3D-Micromac** was the more obvious adjacent comparator in solar, wafer and brittle-material processing. Its own market materials placed the company across photovoltaic and semiconductor production, display-and-smart-glass manufacturing, electronics manufacturing, medical technology and ophthalmic optics, while product literature highlighted solar-cell laser processing and TLS-based wafer dicing. That made 3D-Micromac particularly relevant to the edges of LPKF's Solar and display/glass work, even if it was not marketing a public LIDE-style wet-etch-through-glass-via stack. [3D-Micromac markets](<https://3d-micromac.com/laser-micromachining/markets/>), [3D-Micromac microCELL](<https://3d-micromac.com/microcell>)

**MKS Instruments**, through ESI, remained more clearly tied to conventional PCB-scale laser drilling. Its CapStone system was marketed as a high-speed flex-PCB UV laser-via-drilling platform, which put it closer to mainstream PCB manufacturing equipment than to LPKF's glass-core route. The overlap with LPKF was therefore real in precision laser processing, but the product-market focus was materially different. [MKS ESI CapStone](<https://esi.d1.mks.com/f/capstone-laser-system>)

What distinguishes LPKF within this micromachining constellation is the combination of vertical application focus and process-IP moat. LDS — Laser Direct Structuring, applied to three-dimensional moulded interconnect devices — remains LPKF's most durable competitive asset in electronics. The process, in which a laser selectively activates a catalyst-doped polymer surface to enable selective copper plating, underpins the antenna-in-housing designs prevalent in mobile devices, hearing aids, and automotive radar sensors. Competitors have attempted to develop analogous direct-structuring chemistries, but LPKF's patent portfolio and its co-development relationships with resin suppliers have maintained meaningful barriers. Revenue from LDS systems and licence arrangements has, historically, been the electronics segment's primary driver, though unit volumes are sensitive to the consumer-electronics capex cycle.

## PCB Prototyping: Dominant in a Shrinking Room

The benchtop PCB prototyping market presents a more complicated picture. LPKF's ProtoMat systems have for decades been the instrument of choice in university electronics labs, corporate R&D departments, and defence contractors that require rapid, in-house circuit-board iteration without depending on external fabrication services. The company claims dominant share in this segment globally, a position enabled by its combination of mechanical milling capability, laser structuring options, and an ecosystem of software (CircuitPro) designed for the electronics engineer rather than the fabrication specialist.

The structural headwind is plain. The emergence of low-cost Asian PCB fabrication services — with online platforms offering two-day turnaround on two-layer boards for single-digit dollars — has materially compressed the economic case for in-house prototyping at small quantities. For startups and university labs working on standard FR4 designs, the calculus has tilted toward outsourcing even early iterations. LPKF's response has been to emphasise the segments where in-house prototyping retains operational necessity: classified defence programmes where exporting design files is prohibited; applications requiring same-day or same-hour iteration cycles; and advanced-substrate work — flexible circuits, high-frequency PTFE laminates, and multilayer constructions — where standard fabs require minimum quantities or long lead times.

The competitive roster in this niche is thin. **T-Tech** (US) and **MITS Electronics** (Japan) manufacture competing benchtop milling and routing systems, but neither has matched LPKF's global installed base, software integration, or dealer network depth.
